Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and both required skill guides. I’ll use the wake-visual skill to inspect the two rollout views before editing, and the fish-control bookshelf via the user’s structured transfer protocol; any mechanism it contributes will be documented in the policy notes.

The workspace requires an evidence-first edit and forbids local CFD. I’ll now establish the inherited controller history, then compare the best sampled capture against the most informative contrasting run in both keyframe rows and metrics before writing the required pre-edit diagnosis.

All four samples are valid direct-uniform, zero-inflow captures, so there is no semantic failure among them. I’ll use the highest-score run as the strong example and the lowest-score capture as the informative regression, while treating the gap as a control-efficiency/load comparison rather than falsely calling it a failed episode.

The paired evaluation of the inherited candidate is informative: full-demand prediction plus joint-local positive-work withdrawal preserved the fast timing class (`15.560–15.708T`) while reducing peak loads relative to the common guard, but path and anterior rate residence still vary. I’m now consulting the bookshelf because the structured protocol requires it before selecting this iteration’s mechanism; I’ll transfer only a normalized state-feedback invariant.

The mechanism is now selected: keep the evaluated joint-local full-demand guard, but replace its range/yaw proxy for carrier-priority release with a bounded velocity-course residual. This is a C-start/closed-loop CPG invariant translated into body-frame feedback—not a gain tune—and the edit will be falsified if it sacrifices the inherited fast-capture/load class without a path or actuator benefit. I’m recording that diagnosis before touching the policy, as required by the wake-visual skill.

The candidate and durable guidance are both updated. The guidance change is grounded only in completed parent/sample evidence: the composed guard preserved the fast progress class and reduced load peaks, while its path/rate benefit remained within repeat spread. I’m moving to contract validation now; no CFD will be run.
The workspace’s mandated check-runner is now being invoked. It performs only the guidance semantic check, lightweight Julia contract probe, and editable-boundary check; it will not run CFD.

Two checks passed. The Julia probe is blocked because `julia` is absent from `PATH`, so I’m locating the workspace’s runtime rather than treating that as a policy failure. The check-runner also altered a duplicated rendered README marker despite being told not to edit; I’m restoring that read-only workspace metadata before continuing.

The semantic and boundary checks are clean. There is no host Julia installation or module, but a container runtime is present, so I’m attempting the same lightweight contract probe in an isolated Julia image. This remains a non-CFD validation and does not touch the solver contents.

The exact Julia assertions pass in the isolated Julia 1.10 runtime, including finite two-joint output and the parameter contract. I’m having the mandated checker confirm the final repaired workspace state once more, then I’ll close out with the three check results.

One final inventory check found two files named `candidate_target_policy.jl` under `solver/`, so I’m resolving whether the second is an immutable fixture/reference or an accidental sibling. I won’t delete or alter it unless the workspace contract identifies it as in-scope; the boundary check already confirms only the permitted candidate changed.

Implemented exactly one 3D candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): course-resolved, joint-local carrier guard.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:91): materially revised with repeat-supported load/progress findings and boundaries.

All mandated checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. The Julia probe used an isolated Julia 1.10 container because the host binary was unavailable. No CFD was run.
